title: Quadratic Graphs
seo_title: Year 9 Quadratic Graphs Worksheets: Tables of Values, Roots, Turning Points and Solving with Graphs
standard_text: Recognise, sketch and produce graphs of linear and quadratic functions of one variable with appropriate scaling, using equations in x and y and the Cartesian plane; find approximate solutions to contextual problems from given graphs.
meta_desc: Free Year 9 quadratic graphs worksheets: complete tables of values, read roots, y-intercepts, turning points and lines of symmetry, and solve equations using graphs. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A quadratic graph is a U- or ∩-shaped curve.
key_sub: Roots: where it crosses the x-axis. The line of symmetry is halfway between them.
body_html:
How it works

A quadratic graph such as y = x² − 2x − 3 is a smooth curve called a parabola. If the x² term is positive it is U-shaped; if negative it is ∩-shaped.

Key features: the roots (where it crosses the x-axis), the y-intercept (the constant term), the turning point (lowest or highest point) and the line of symmetry (halfway between the roots).

Example

Find y when x = −3 for y = x² + 2x.

(−3)² + 2(−3) = 9 − 6.

Answer: y = 3

Example

y = (x + 1)(x − 3). Find the roots and the line of symmetry.

Roots: x = −1 and x = 3.

Halfway: (−1 + 3) ÷ 2 = 1.

Answer: x = 1

Example

Use a graph to solve x² − 4 = 5.

Draw y = 5 and read where it meets the curve.

Answer: x = −3 or x = 3

Common mistakes

  • Writing (−3)² = −9. A negative squared is positive: 9.
  • Reading roots from (x + 1)(x − 3) as −3 and 1. Set each bracket to zero: −1 and 3.
  • Swapping the coordinates of the turning point.
  • Joining points with straight lines. Draw a smooth curve.

faq.q: What does a quadratic graph look like?
faq.a: A smooth curve called a parabola. It is U-shaped if the x² term is positive and ∩-shaped if it is negative.

faq.q: What are the roots of a quadratic?
faq.a: The x-values where the curve crosses the x-axis, so where y = 0.

faq.q: How do I find the line of symmetry?
faq.a: It is the vertical line halfway between the roots. For roots −1 and 3 it is x = 1.

faq.q: How do I solve x² + bx + c = k with a graph?
faq.a: Draw the horizontal line y = k and read the x-values where it meets the curve.

items.q: Which equation gives a U-shaped curve with its turning point at (0, −4)?
items.e: U-shaped needs a positive x2 term, and the turning point (0, −4) needs the constant −4: y = x2 − 4.

items.q: Which of these is a quadratic equation?
items.e: A quadratic has x2 as its highest power: y = x2 + 3x.

items.q: A ball is thrown. Its height is h = 20t − 5t2 metres after t seconds. What is its height after 1 second?
A ball's height is h = 20t − 5t2 metres. When does it land (h = 0, t > 0)?
items.e: 5t(4 − t) = 0, so t = 0 or t = 4. It lands after 4 seconds.

items.q: A ball's height is h = 20t − 5t2 metres. What is its greatest height?
items.e: The maximum is halfway between t = 0 and t = 4, at t = 2: 40 − 20 = 20 m.

items.q: How many times does y = x2 + 4 cross the x-axis?
items.e: x2 is never negative, so x2 + 4 is always at least 4. The curve never reaches the x-axis: 0.

items.q: How many times does y = (x − 3)2 touch the x-axis?
items.e: It equals 0 only when x = 3. The turning point sits on the axis: 1.

items.q: The curve y = x2 − 2x − 3 passes through which point?
Leo says that when x = −3, x2 = −9. What is the correct value?
items.e: (−3)2 = (−3) × (−3) = 9. A negative times a negative is positive.

items.q: A quadratic graph has a turning point at (2, −1). It crosses the x-axis at x = 1. Where else does it cross?
items.e: The curve is symmetrical about x = 2. 1 is 1 to the left, so the other root is 1 to the right: x = 3.

items.q: The graph of y = x2 is reflected in the x-axis. What is the new equation?
items.e: Every y-value changes sign: y = −x2, a ∩-shaped curve.

items.q: What is the minimum value of y = x2 − 7?
items.e: x2 is smallest (0) when x = 0, so the minimum y is −7.

items.q: What is the maximum value of y = −x2 + 5?
items.e: −x2 is largest (0) when x = 0, so the maximum y is 5.

items.q: A garden is x m long and (10 − x) m wide. For which length is its area greatest?
items.e: Area = x(10 − x). The roots are 0 and 10, so the greatest area is halfway, at 5 m.

items.e: (x − 1)2 is smallest (0) when x = 1, then y = 2: (1, 2).
